toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The rise is very likely not a handling problem. Since 1 September, tags printed on the new Fennick stock fail automatic reading about 12% of the time, against about 1.5% before. Those bags go to the manual encode desk, where waits rose from 7 to about 30 minutes in the evening bank. They reach the lateral after the cart has closed and miss the flight. Bags that read automatically are as reliable as before (about 3.8 per 1,000). Pelion, handled by the same Tessaly crew pool, did not worsen. On 14–16 Oct, counters briefly using old Brackwater stock failed at 1.6% while kiosks on Fennick failed at 12.1%. Transfer tags and Pelion tags read normally, so the airport's readers are not at fault.

What is unclear is whether the stock itself is faulty or whether the printers need different heat settings for it. Kiosk cleaning also became less frequent.

Next steps: do not send the breach notice or withhold the fee. Switch back to Brackwater stock now (about five weeks are in stores and the contract is valid to 31 Dec). Then test Fennick stock with the printer maker's settings before making any claim against Fennick. Asking HBAA for an extra encode workstation in the evening is a reasonable stopgap. I'm fairly confident in this.
